correctness.rationale: For connected unlabeled graphs of orders 2,3,4,5 (exact class counts 1,2,6,21), the finite edge-subset identity calculates every risk as an integer polynomial divided by n-1. Exhaustive label-permutation reduction and the transform p=t/(1+t) provide 127 exact coefficientwise nonnegative comparisons certifying a permanent optimum for every class other than two. On the two exceptional adjacency lists, fully explicit factored polynomial differences show exact optimizer sets on both sides of p=1/4 and dominance over all other vertices. A separate pair-connectivity evaluator agrees in 147 integer-polynomial checks. These are exhaustive over the finite domain, not samples, and the executable standard-library verifier reproduces the algebra and graph census.

value.rationale: A complete minimal-size classification addresses when degree- or structure-only one-dose vaccination rankings can remain optimal across transmission regimes. The two first counterexamples occur at the sharp smallest order n=5, each with an exact p=1/4 crossover between same-degree nodes. This is a natural complete finite invariant with clear uses as a benchmark for parameter-sensitive vaccination heuristics and exact infection-spread solvers. The result does not claim policy effectiveness outside its mathematical assumptions.
